subject: Understanding India
text: Read the following case study and answer the following questions:   6 Mother Tongue-Based Education under NEP 2020 The National Education Policy 2020 introduced a major reform by recommending the mother tongue or local language as the medium of instruction in early education, especially up to Grade 5. This policy aims to make education more holistic, inclusive, and effective in India’s multilingual society. In many Indian schools, especially in rural and tribal areas, children were taught in English or Hindi, which were not their first languages. This created learning difficulties, low confidence poor academic performance, and higher dropout rates. Students often felt disconnected from their culture and learning environment. NEP 2020 promoted mother tongue-based education, along with the three-language formula (mother tongue, Hindi, and English). Teachers were trained to teach in local languages, and efforts were made to develop textbooks and digital learning materials in regional languages. The goal was to improve comprehension, preserve cultural identity, and ensure inclusive education. Mother tongue education helped students understand concepts more easily improved confidence, and enhanced creativity and critical thinking. It also strengthened cultural identity, emotional stability, and social responsibility. This approach reduced educational disparities, especially among rural, tribal, and marginalized students, and promoted equitable access to education. The policy faced challenges such as shortage of trained teachers, lack of teaching materials in local languages, and parental preference for English-medium education. Developing resources for many languages was also complex and costly. Mother tongue-based education under NEP 2020 has the potential to improve learning outcomes, preserve linguistic diversity, and promote inclusive and holistic development. With proper implementation, teacher training, and awareness, it can transform India’s education system and create confident, culturally rooted and globally competent learners
